<reason>Both sides ran disciplined, on-motion cases. A's route was institutional: a narrow production benchmark is harder to explain away, and a division of labour (growth headline + binding standards + separately reported outcomes) keeps responsibility legible. B's route was mechanistic: the headline is what the Treasury builds cases around and what the press runs, so headlining the instrument produces means-end inversion. B's decisive move was answering A's central "elasticity/discretion" charge twice over — first that GDP is itself stuffed with contested conventions and routinely spun (aggregate vs per capita, one-off shocks), and second that life satisfaction's weights are set by respondents, not ministers, so they cannot be reset by accounting revision. A never squarely rebutted that non-manipulability point. A did land a real hit under pressure: B's mean-plus-floor specification still lacks a priority rule when average and low-end diverge, and B effectively conceded this. But B's reframe — GDP silently resolves that question by assigning zero, so contestation belongs in public view — absorbed the hit rather than collapsing under it. A's other strongest strands (growth expands fiscal capacity; short-termism) were largely neutralised by B's concession that welfare-raising growth is still rewarded, and A's counter that future tenants cannot report today was a fair but partial dent. A also carried the weight of its own opening concession that well-being is the purpose, and its answer to "ministers follow the headline" stayed at the level of assertion. B's turn was clipped for length, a genuine execution cost, but the lost text was peroration rather than substance.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B's reply to the elasticity charge: GDP's own conventions (imputed rent, zero-valued unpaid care, forests as income) are contested and already spun by governments, whereas subjective well-being "cannot be conjured with an accounting revision" because respondents do the weighting. Paired with "implicit weights are unexamined weights, which is worse," this turned A's central objection into a point against GDP, and A never fully answered it.</best_rebuttal>
